record.original_question: Define anisotropic function spaces adapted to ideal hydrodynamics that have higher regularity along flow lines than across them, and prove existence and uniqueness theorems for Euler dynamics in those spaces in any dimension.

evidence.quote: Problem 16. Define anisotropic spaces more appropriate for hydrodynamics with larger smooth- ness in the direction of flow lines. Prove existence and uniqueness theorems for ideal hydrody- namics in those function spaces in any dimension. The concept of GM-flows appears closely related to the “ancient flows” for the Navier–Stokes equations but, in fact, it is different. Both concepts express the general idea that, in reality, we observe flows that have existed since long time ago (one may imagine a river flow). In this regard, it is not natural to consider flows starting at some definite time t0 with some (arbitrary) initial velocity u0 . GM-flows have natural, intrinsic structure (analytic level lines of vorticity) and some natural, finite regularity in the transversal direction. The question of which functional classes are suitable for their study is an intriguing open problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the incompressible Euler equations for an ideal fluid on $\mathbb{R}^d$ (or on a smooth $d$-dimensional Riemannian manifold), $d \ge 2$:
$$\partial_t u + (u\cdot\nabla) u + \nabla p = 0,\qquad \operatorname{div} u = 0,$$
where $u(t,x)$ is the velocity field and $p(t,x)$ the pressure.

Motivated by the observation that physical fluid flows often exhibit much higher smoothness along streamlines (integral curves of $u$) than transverse to them — for example, vorticity tends to be analytic along level lines while only finitely smooth in the transverse direction — carry out the following program:

(a) Define a scale of anisotropic function spaces $X = X(\Omega)$ on a domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ (or on a manifold) in which regularity is measured separately in the direction tangent to the flow lines of a given divergence-free vector field $u$ and in the directions transverse to those flow lines, with strictly higher (e.g., analytic or Gevrey) regularity required tangentially and only finite (e.g., Hölder or Sobolev) regularity required transversally. Provide a precise definition of $X$ that is intrinsic, invariant under volume-preserving diffeomorphisms compatible with the flow structure, and well adapted to the transport operator $u\cdot\nabla$.

(b) Prove local-in-time existence and uniqueness theorems for the Euler system above with initial data in $X$, in any dimension $d \ge 2$, establishing that the solution map $u_0 \mapsto u(t,\cdot)$ is well-defined and continuous in the topology of $X$ on some nontrivial time interval.
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution of this program was found. The literature contains related work on anisotropic Hölder/Sobolev spaces in fluid problems and on Lagrangian flows with anisotropic regularity, but no construction of intrinsic anisotropic function spaces with higher tangential regularity along streamlines together with corresponding existence/uniqueness theorems for the Euler equations in arbitrary dimension. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Lagrangian flows for vector fields with anisotropic regularity
status_evidence.snippet: Quantitative estimates for flows of vector fields with anisotropic regularity conditions, enabling well-posedness of transport and continuity equations.
status_evidence.claim: Related anisotropic-regularity results for transport exist, but do not provide intrinsic spaces with higher tangential smoothness for the Euler system.

status_evidence.title: Strong illposedness of the incompressible Euler equation in integer C^m spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Illposedness results in standard isotropic spaces motivate searching for better-adapted anisotropic function classes.
status_evidence.claim: Standard isotropic spaces are known to be inadequate, but a successful anisotropic replacement adapted to flow lines has not been established.
